title: Array
intuition: A contiguous sequence of memory cells accessed instantly by numeric index.
whyExists: Computers store data in RAM addressed sequentially. If you need instantaneous random access to items by their offset without following pointers, contiguous memory is required.
analogy: Imagine a row of numbered mailboxes in an apartment lobby: knowing box #5 lets you walk directly to it without inspecting boxes 1 through 4.
coreIdea: An Array allocates a contiguous block of memory where each element occupies a fixed number of bytes. The address of element i is computed by baseAddress + i * elementSize in $O(1)$ time. Inserting or deleting in the middle requires shifting trailing elements, costing $O(n)$ time.

complexity.reason: Direct pointer arithmetic yields O(1) random access; element shifts dominate dynamic resizing.

pitfalls: Off-by-one errors when iterating from index 0 to length - 1.
Buffer overflow / IndexOutOfBoundsException when accessing indices outside [0, n - 1].
High cost of middle insertions due to bulk element copying.
